meanings.note: Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: البنت المشهورة describes Layan's high-profile popularity across school.

examples.trans: Layan is well-known across the whole school.
This is a famous restaurant in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (formal هنا).

examples.trans: Come sit here next to me.
Life is very sweet here.

meanings.note: Central setting: مدرسة الروابي للبنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls').

examples.trans: The school is close to our house.
I like going to school early.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun, كل means 'every' (كل يوم، كل إشي); with الـ (الكل) it means 'everyone'; with suffixes (كلنا، كلهم، كلها) 'all of us/them/it'.

examples.trans: Everyone knows the story.
We see each other every day.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: Past tense linking verb (كنت، كنتي، كان، كنا) and subjunctive تكون / نكون ('to be'); ما كان عندي means 'I didn't have'.

examples.trans: I was at school in the morning.
Today was very long.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun endings مني (from me), منها (of/from her), منكم (of you): تكون من شلتها ('be part of her clique'), بخاف منها ('afraid of her').

examples.trans: I got off the bus.
Which one of you saw what happened?

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tight-knit school clique (شلتها 'her clique').

examples.trans: The whole school knows Layan's clique.
I sat with my friend group at recess.

meanings.note: Placed before a definite noun without changing form: بنفس الغرفة ('in the same room'), بنفس الوقت ('at the same time').

examples.trans: We ride the same bus.
We arrived at the same time.

meanings.note: Versatile noun: ما عندي وقت ('no time'), صار الوقت ('it's time'), وقتها ('at that moment / then'), مش وقته ('not the time for it').

examples.trans: I didn't have time to explain.
Everything is nice in its own time.

meanings.note: Construes with من for the person or thing feared (بخاف منها 'fears her').

examples.trans: I'm not afraid of anyone.
Don't be afraid, I'm with you.

meanings.note: Warm or emphatic 'of course', used seriously or playfully between friends.

examples.trans: Of course I'll help you.
Of course I know the answer.

meanings.note: Used idiomatically in بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('takes her very seriously / fears crossing her').

examples.trans: We calculated the time exactly.
Count me in with you.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative base taking pronoun endings: إلي (to me), إلك (to you), إلها (to her), إلنا (for us), إلهم (to them).

examples.trans: This book is for you.
Tell me the truth.

meanings.note: In بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('counts a thousand accounts for her'), ألف intensifies caution: everyone thinks twice around her.

examples.trans: I thought about it a thousand times.
Thanks a thousand times.

meanings.note: In عمل/حسب ألف حساب, means thinking very carefully before crossing someone.

examples.trans: Everyone thinks twice around her.
That wasn't part of the calculation.

meanings.note: Versatile Levantine word meaning 'but' between clauses and 'only / just' inside a clause.
As a focus adverb before a verb, noun, or imperative, بس narrows or softens the statement.

examples.trans: I tried to speak, but she didn't hear me.
I just want one minute.

meanings.note: Independent first-person singular pronoun for any gender.

examples.trans: I am a student at the school.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Negates past and b-present verbs (ما إجيت، ما بعرف) and idioms like ما عليكم ('never mind'); after قبل or بدل (قبل ما، بدل ما) it links a verb clause.

examples.trans: I didn't hear the bell.
Come before the school closes.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine indefinite person word; ما حدا means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Is anyone in the classroom?
Nobody believed me.

meanings.note: Polite 'yes' to a teacher (نعم يا مس), or a sharp rising 'Excuse me?!' (نعم؟) when someone feels challenged.

examples.trans: Yes Miss, I'm here.
Excuse me? Repeat what you just said!

meanings.note: Spoken feminine singular 'you', spelled with final ي to reflect the Jordanian pronunciation inti.

examples.trans: Are you a new girl here?
What do you think?

meanings.note: Placed before a b-present verb (عم بكذبوا، عم بتتحديني) to spotlight an action happening right now.

examples.trans: The girls are studying in the library right now.
What are you saying?

meanings.note: With progressive عم (عم بتتحديني؟), Layan asks 'are you challenging me right now?'.

examples.trans: Nobody challenges her at school.
Are you challenging me?

meanings.note: Placed before a name or title whenever addressing someone directly (يا دينا، يا مس فاتن); natural English usually drops it.

examples.trans: Come here, Mariam.
Thank you very much, Miss.

meanings.note: Core Levantine question word for 'what?' (شو صار؟) and casual conversation starter ('So, ...').

examples.trans: What are you doing here?
So, ready to go?

meanings.note: Active participle of وقف used for present posture (ليان واقفة، أنا واقفة بمكاني).

examples.trans: Why are you standing by the door?
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: With possessive -ي: مكاني ('my place / my spot').

examples.trans: School is my favorite place.
Stay standing in your spot.

meanings.note: Asks about manner or state (كيف كان الفيلم؟ 'how was the movie?', شفت كيف... 'I saw how...').

examples.trans: How are you today?
How did you get here?

meanings.note: Used in بتوقف بطريقها ('stands in her way') and كيف بتوقفي بوجهي ('how dare you stand in my face').

examples.trans: She stood by me during the trouble.
The bus stopped in front of the school.

meanings.note: In بتوقفي بوجهي ('you stand in my face'), expresses open defiance.

examples.trans: Upset showed on her face.
I told the truth to her face.

meanings.note: With هـ + الـ, بهالطريقة means 'in this way / like that'.

examples.trans: I don't like you talking to me in this way.
We found an easy way to solve it.

meanings.note: Covers transitive 'push someone away' (أبعدها عني) and the everyday imperative ابعدي ('step away').

examples.trans: Step out of my way.
I wanted to push her away from me.

meanings.note: Marks topics (عني 'about me'), distance (ابعدي عن طريقي 'away from my path'), and defense (بيدافعوا عنها 'defend her').

examples.trans: We talked about the movie yesterday.
Stay away from her, please.

meanings.note: Used literally and figuratively: بطريقها ('in her way') and ابعدي عن طريقي ('step out of my way').

examples.trans: Step out of my way, please.
The way to school is short.

meanings.note: Introduces conditions (لو ضلت معهم 'if she stays with them'), concessions (حتى لو 'even if'), and polite لو سمحتي ('please').

examples.trans: If I knew, I would have told you.
Help me, please.

meanings.note: In the polite request لو سمحت / لو سمحتي ('if you allowed' = please), addressed to a woman with -تي.

examples.trans: Open the window, please.
The teacher doesn't allow lateness.

meanings.note: Imperative feminine اسمعي منيح ('listen closely'); past سمعت ('she heard / I heard').

examples.trans: Listen to what I want to tell you.
I heard every word they said.

meanings.note: Core Levantine word (mniih) used adverbially after verbs of knowing or listening: عارفة منيح ('know very well'), اسمعي منيح ('listen well').

examples.trans: Listen to me well, Noaf.
I know the story well.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine future marker placed before a bare subjunctive verb (رح أخلص، ما رح نسكت).

examples.trans: I'm going to tell the truth.
I won't forget this day.

meanings.note: Form II verb (dammar): أنا رح أدمرك ('I am going to ruin you').

examples.trans: Lying destroys trust.
She thought she could ruin me.

meanings.note: Before لو (حتى لو 'even if'), introduces an extreme condition.

examples.text: رح أحكي الصدق حتى لو زعلوا.
examples.trans: I'll tell the truth even if they get upset.
She didn't even say hello to me.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine demonstrative used before a definite noun (هاد الإشي، هاد الحكي) or as a pronoun (حتى لو هاد آخر إشي).

examples.trans: Is this book yours?
This isn't fair at all.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite singular noun (آخر مرة 'the last time', آخر إشي 'the last thing') without changing for gender.

examples.trans: This is the last time.
This is the last thing I have.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian word corresponding to formal شيء; definite form الإشي, plural أشياء.

examples.trans: There is something important I want to say.
Nothing happened.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'do' or 'make' (بعمل وظيفة 'doing homework', بعملوا مشاكل 'making trouble').

examples.trans: How did you do on the exam?
I didn't do anything wrong.

meanings.note: With a possessive suffix, التاء المربوطة opens to ت: بحياتي ('in my life').

examples.trans: Life is sweet with friends.
I've never seen anything like that in my life.

meanings.note: Invariable Levantine relative pronoun replacing الذي / التي / الذين and 'what' (اللي صار 'what happened').

examples.trans: The girl whom I saw is my friend.
Tell me what happened.

meanings.note: Levantine 'want' built from بد- plus pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بدنا (we want).

examples.trans: What do you want to do now?
I wanted to talk with you.

meanings.note: Carries a direct-object pronoun after pseudo-verbs like بدي: اللي بدك إياه ('whatever you want [it]').

examples.trans: Take whatever you want.
I gave it to you yesterday.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech mainly in fixed polite phrases like إلى اللقاء! ('Until next time!').

examples.trans: Until next time, girls!
We reached the end of the lesson.

meanings.note: Used in the warm standard farewell إلى اللقاء! ('Until we meet again! / Until next time!').

examples.trans: Until next time soon!
It was a very nice meeting.
